body: {"total":2,"records":[{"title":"Telephone and text support for attendance at community strength and balance classes: a pragmatic trial","authors":"Lindberg-Okafor A, Marsh-Venkataraman T, Oduya-Clarke P","year":2022,"venue":"Kestrelmoor Journal of Ageing and Activity","doi":"10.5555/kjaa.2022.0147","providerType":"journal-article","abstract":"We allocated 412 adults aged 65 and over who were joining community strength and balance classes either to usual classes or to classes with weekly text or phone reminders and a call after any missed week. Attendance at two thirds or more of sessions over 24 weeks was 54 percent with support and 41 percent with usual classes. Falls over 12 months did not differ between groups (rate ratio 0.94, 95 percent CI 0.71 to 1.25). Participants valued calls more than texts, and people without a mobile phone received calls only. The trial was not blinded, and instructors knew which participants received support."},{"title":"Peer volunteer calls and home exercise after falls prevention classes: a controlled comparison in community programmes","authors":"Achterberg-Moyo S, Fernandez-Hale R","year":2018,"venue":"Ashcombe Community Rehabilitation Reports","providerType":"journal-article","abstract":"Two community falls prevention programmes offered participants two calls from a trained peer volunteer, a former participant, while a third programme did not. Home exercise diaries were completed on at least three days a week by 62 percent of participants who received peer calls and 35 percent of those who did not. Attendance at classes was similar in the three programmes. Peer volunteers reported that the calls were rewarding but that some participants were hard to reach. Programmes were not allocated at random, the diaries were self-reported, and the programme that offered no calls served an older population."}]}
